oneLiner: 专制、民主与放任——勒温用实验让孩子体验：民主组质量更高，专制组更快却更脆。
oneLinerEn: Autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire — Lewin's experiments with children: democracy gave quality, autocracy speed but fragility.
detail: 库尔特·勒温 (1939) 把成年人带到后台，让同一批孩子分别由三种风格的“领导”带领做手工。专制组效率高但敌意与依赖强，领导一走就乱;民主组更有创造力与满意度，能自我维持;放任组最散漫、产出最低。风格没有绝对对错，但它确实塑造着群体的气氛与韧性。
detailEn: Kurt Lewin (1939) had adults lead the same children's arts group under three styles from behind a curtain. Autocratic clusters were productive but hostile and dependent — they fell apart when the leader left. Democratic ones showed more creativity and satisfaction and sustained themselves. Laissez-faire was the least productive. No style is universally right, but each shapes the group's climate and resilience.

oneLiner: 对新手多给指令，对专家多给授权——风格要随下属的能力与意愿切换。
oneLinerEn: Direct the novice, delegate to the expert — shift style with the follower's competence and commitment.
detail: 赫塞与布兰查德主张，有效的领导没有固定套路，只有四种模式沿“指令—教练—支持—授权”的光谱移动，随下属对特定任务的“成熟度”(能力 + 意愿)而选。同一位员工在不同任务上、在不同阶段，可能需要完全不同的对待。它直觉好用，但也因难以严格验证而受过学理批评。
detailEn: Hersey and Blanchard held there is no single right style, only four modes along a telling—selling—participating—delegating spectrum, chosen by the follower's readiness (competence plus commitment) for the specific task. The same person may need different handling across tasks and over time. Intuitively useful, it has been criticised as hard to validate rigorously.

oneLiner: 领导效能 = 领导风格 × 情境控制力的匹配度。
oneLinerEn: Leadership effectiveness is the match between a leader's style and the control the situation offers.
detail: 菲德勒用“最难共事同事(LPC)”量表衡量领导者是任务导向还是关系导向，再用上下级关系、任务结构、职位权力三项判断情境控制力。结论带有挑战性：任务导向者在极端有利或极端不利的处境表现更好，关系导向者在中间处境更好。而且他认为风格相对稳定，与其试图“改造人”，不如“把合适的人放到合适的岗位，或把情境改造成匹配领导”。
detailEn: Fiedler gauged whether a leader is task- or relationship-oriented with the 'Least Preferred Coworker' scale, then judged situational control from leader-member relations, task structure and position power. The conclusion was provocative: task leaders do best in situations either very favourable or very unfavourable, relationship leaders in the middle. And since he saw style as fairly fixed, he argued for matching the person to the situation — or reshaping the situation — rather than trying to rewire the person.

oneLiner: 交易型用奖惩交换绩效，变革型靠愿景、激发与关怀提升动机层次。
oneLinerEn: Transactional leaders trade rewards for performance; transformational ones raise motive through vision, stimulation and care.
detail: 伯恩斯奠基、巴斯发展：交易型领导明确“做到就给、做不到就罚”，在稳定任务中有效;变革型领导通过理想化的榜样、鼓舞人心的愿景、智力激发(鼓励质疑)与个性化关怀(因材施教)，把追随者从“为了报酬”推向“为了意义”。大量研究显示变革型与更高的绩效、承诺和满意度相关——但它需要真诚，否则易滑向作秀。
detailEn: Burns laid the groundwork, Bass developed it. Transactional leadership spells out 'deliver and be rewarded, fall short and be corrected' and works well on stable tasks. Transformational leadership uses idealised example, an inspiring vision, intellectual stimulation and individualised consideration to move followers from reward to meaning. Much research links it to higher performance, commitment and satisfaction — but it demands sincerity or it slides into theatre.

oneLiner: 生理、安全、归属、尊重、自我实现——未满足的低层需求主导行为。
oneLinerEn: Physiological, safety, belonging, esteem, self-actualisation: the lowest unsatisfied need drives behaviour.
detail: 亚伯拉罕·马斯洛 (1943) 把人的需求画成阶梯，主张低层相对满足后才向上追求。它对管理的启示很直接:饿着肚子或担心被裁的人，很难被“自我实现”的口号打动。它也常被批评:证据基础薄弱、分层过于刚性、带有西方个人主义色彩——把它当作提醒而非精确模型更稳妥。
detailEn: Abraham Maslow (1943) stacked human needs, holding that we pursue higher ones only once lower ones are relatively met. The managerial punch is blunt: people who are hungry or fearing the axe are not moved by appeals to self-actualisation. It is criticised for a thin evidence base, too-rigid tiers and a Western individualist slant — best used as a prompt, not a precise model.

oneLiner: 保健因素消除不满，激励因素带来满意——“满意”的反面不是“不满意”。
oneLinerEn: Hygiene removes dissatisfaction; motivators create satisfaction — the opposite of satisfaction is not dissatisfaction.
detail: 赫茨伯格访谈会计师与工程师后发现:薪资、政策、监督、条件等“保健因素”不足会让人不满，但把它们做好也只是“不再不满”，并不会真正点燃动力;真正带来满意与投入的是成就、认可、责任、成长与工作本身这些“激励因素”。这解释了为什么单纯加薪买不来长期敬业——它是止痛药，不是维生素。
detailEn: Interviewing accountants and engineers, Herzberg found that hygiene factors — pay, policy, supervision, conditions — when lacking breed dissatisfaction, but perfected only yield 'not dissatisfied', never true drive. Satisfaction and engagement come from motivators: achievement, recognition, the work itself, responsibility and growth. Hence a pay raise alone won't buy lasting engagement — it is a painkiller, not a vitamin.

term: 麦格雷戈 X-Y 理论
oneLiner: 你假设人惰性逃避(X)还是自主负责(Y)，制度与控制风格会被这个假设自我实现。
oneLinerEn: Assume people shirk (X) or own their work (Y), and your systems make that assumption come true.
detail: 道格拉斯·麦格雷戈 (1960) 指出:持 X 假设的管理者会搭严密的监控、惩罚与集权，恰恰把人逼得消极;持 Y 假设者会给自主、参与与成长，往往激发出责任感。它是“假设会自我实现”的经典表述。后续更谨慎的 Z 理论(威廉·大内)与情境观点提醒:人不是非 X 即 Y，管理方式要看任务、文化与个人。
detailEn: Douglas McGregor (1960) argued that managers who assume Theory X build tight surveillance, punishment and centralisation — which duly makes people passive; those who assume Theory Y grant autonomy, participation and growth, and often draw out ownership. It is a classic statement that assumptions self-fulfil. Later, more careful views — Theory Z (Ouchi) and contingency — remind us people are not simply X or Y and style must fit task, culture and person.

oneLiner: 动力 = 努力能达绩效 × 绩效能得报酬 × 报酬对我有价值；任一为零，激励归零。
oneLinerEn: Motivation = expectancy × instrumentality × valence; if any term is zero, motivation collapses.
detail: 维克托·弗鲁姆 (1964) 把激励拆成三个心理判断:我相信努力能换来好绩效吗(期望)?好绩效真会换来承诺的回报吗(工具性)?那回报是我想要的吗(效价)?这条链条把“为什么画大饼没用”讲得极清楚——只要员工不信、或奖励自己压根不在乎，激励力就乘成了零。管理者的抓手，就是逐环把这三问坐实。
detailEn: Victor Vroom (1964) decomposed motivation into three beliefs: will effort yield performance (expectancy), will performance yield the promised reward (instrumentality), and is that reward something I value (valence)? It states crisply why empty promises fail — if staff disbelieve any link, or do not want the prize, the product is zero. The manager's job is to make each link real.

oneLiner: 人会把自己的“得/付出”和参照对象比；一旦觉得亏待，就想办法把它扳平。
oneLinerEn: People compare their outcomes-to-inputs with a referent; feel shortchanged and they act to restore balance.
detail: 斯塔西·亚当斯认为公平是主观感知:你算出自己的“产出 ÷ 投入”，再与同事或同行比较，若感到被亏待，就会设法恢复平衡——少干活、要求加薪、在心里换一个参照对象，或者干脆离开。它对管理的启示是:绝对数额常常不如“相对公平感”重要;因此薪酬透明与程序公正(怎么决定的、可不可申诉)格外关键。
detailEn: J. Stacy Adams held that equity is a perception: you compute your outcomes over inputs, compare it with a colleague or market referent, and — feeling under-rewarded — act to restore balance: slack off, demand more, quietly switch referents, or leave. The lesson for managers is that relative fairness often matters more than absolute pay, so pay transparency and procedural justice (how a decision was made and can it be appealed) are crucial.

oneLiner: 具体而有挑战性、并配反馈的目标，比“尽力就好”更能提升绩效。
oneLinerEn: Specific, challenging goals with feedback beat 'do your best' at driving performance.
detail: 埃德温·洛克(与莱瑟姆)经过大量研究确立:目标通过四条途径起作用——引导注意、调动努力、延长坚持、激发策略探索。前提是员工接受了目标(承诺)、并有能力与反馈支撑。它也有阴暗面:为达成一个醒目数字而牺牲质量、走捷径甚至造假——所以目标要成组(兼顾质量与长期)，并把过程诚信与心理安全感一起设计进去。
detailEn: Edwin Locke (with Latham), across hundreds of studies, established that specific, challenging goals raise performance by directing attention, mobilising effort, sustaining persistence and sparking strategy — provided the person accepts the goal and has the ability and feedback to pursue it. It has a dark side: a lone salient number invites cut corners, quality damage or outright gaming. Hence goals should come in balanced sets, with process integrity and psychological safety designed alongside.

oneLiner: 领导的本职是扫清通往目标的障碍，风格要补下属所缺(指导、支持、参与、成就导向)。
oneLinerEn: The leader's job is to clear the path to goals, choosing a style — directive, supportive, participative, achievement-oriented — that supplies what the subordinate lacks.
detail: 罗伯特·豪斯(1971)把弗鲁姆期望理论与领导行为结合：领导者在下属与目标之间搭桥，按其能力、任务结构与情境，补足缺失的一环——任务模糊就多指导，任务压抑就多支持。它把“哪种风格最好”改写成“此刻这位下属需要什么”，是情境路径的精细化版本。
detailEn: Robert House (1971) fused Vroom's expectancy theory with leadership behaviour: the leader bridges subordinate and goal, and by the person's ability, task structure and setting supplies the missing link — more direction when the task is ambiguous, more support when it is stifling. It rewrites 'which style is best' as 'what this follower needs now', a fine-grained cousin of the situational path.

oneLiner: 领导者与每个下属各建一段关系，有人进“圈内”、有人留在“圈外”，质量决定资源与信任。
oneLinerEn: A leader builds a separate relationship with each subordinate — an in-group and an out-group — whose quality drives trust, latitude and reward.
detail: 格雷恩与比尔(1975)指出领导不是对所有人一视同仁，而是与少数人发展高质量交换(互信、额外机会、影响力)，多数人维持低质量的契约式关系。圈内绩效、满意度、留任更高。它既解释“嫡系”现象，也提醒：偏私若与贡献无关，会侵蚀公平与心理安全。
detailEn: Graen and Uhl-Bien (1975) showed leaders do not treat all alike but build high-quality exchanges (trust, extra opportunity, influence) with a few in-group members while most stay in a lower-quality contractual out-group. The in-group enjoys higher performance, satisfaction and retention. It explains the 'inner circle' and warns that favouritism untethered from contribution erodes equity and psychological safety.

oneLiner: 领导首先是服务者——先满足下属成长与自主，权力自下而上地授予。
oneLinerEn: The leader is first a server — putting subordinates' growth and autonomy first, so authority is granted from below.
detail: 罗伯特·格林利夫(1970)提出“仆人式领导”：领导者先问“团队需要什么”，通过倾听、共情、觉察、说服、管家责任与致力于他人成长来赋能，而非靠职位发号施令。它把变革型的“提升动机”再推进一步——把目的从组织绩效部分转向人的成长，成为后来谦逊领导、赋能管理的源头。
detailEn: Robert Greenleaf (1970) proposed the servant leader, who 'starts with the natural feeling that one wants to serve' — empowering through listening, empathy, awareness, persuasion, stewardship and commitment to people's growth, rather than commanding from the chair. It pushes transformational 'elevating motive' a step further, shifting part of the purpose from organisational performance to human growth, and seeded today's humble and empowering leadership.

term: 管理 4C（清晰·承诺·能力·控制）
oneLiner: 让事情真正发生靠四环：把目标说清晰、拿到真承诺、配得上能力、留得住控制。
oneLinerEn: Getting things done holds on four Cs — Clarity of goal, genuine Commitment, matching Competence and steady Control.
detail: 一条把“管理”落到执行闭环的清单：Clarity 让每个成员对目标与标准有清晰一致的理解，别靠猜；Commitment 是被真正认可而非口头答应的投入，靠参与而非强压；Competence 是把合适的人放在合适的事上并补齐能力缺口；Control 不是微观插手，而是建立可见的进度与纠偏机制，跑偏时及时发现。四者缺一，计划就停在纸面；它常用来诊断“为什么定好的事执行不下去”。
detailEn: A checklist that turns management into an execution loop: Clarity means every member shares a clear, aligned read of the goal rather than guessing; Commitment is engagement genuinely owned, not just verbally agreed, won through involvement rather than pressure; Competence puts the right person on the right task and closes skill gaps; Control is not micromanaging but making progress visible and correctable so drift is caught early. Miss any one and the plan stays on paper — it is a common lens for diagnosing 'why a settled plan fails to get executed'.

oneLiner: 行为由后果决定：被奖励的会重复、被惩罚或忽视的会消退——别谈态度，改后果。
oneLinerEn: Behaviour is shaped by its consequences — what is rewarded recurs, what is punished or ignored fades; change the consequences, not the attitude.
detail: 斯金纳的操作性条件反射被搬到管理：员工的重复行为主要由“之后发生了什么”决定，正强化(及时、具体的表扬与回报)增加行为，负强化(撤掉不快的刺激)也增加行为，惩罚压制行为，消退(不再回应)让其自然减少。它强调即时、明确、可预期，且“抓好的”比“抓错的”更有效；与只讲内在动机的自我决定理论互补——外在胡萝卜对简单可量化的行为立竿见影，对复杂、需要创造与真诚的工作则要慎用，否则易被刷指标、伤内在动机。
detailEn: Skinner's operant conditioning brought into management: repeat behaviour is driven mainly by 'what happened next' — positive reinforcement (timely, specific praise and reward) increases it, negative reinforcement (removing something unpleasant) also increases it, punishment suppresses it, and extinction (withdrawing response) lets it fade. It stresses immediacy, clarity and predictability and that 'catching people doing well' beats 'catching them doing wrong'; it complements self-determination theory, which leans on intrinsic motive — external carrots work fast on simple, measurable behaviour but must be used sparingly on complex, creative, heartfelt work, lest they game the metric and crowd out intrinsic drive.

oneLiner: 从管理自我到管理他人、再管管理者、管职能、管事业部、管集团——每上一级都要换一套工作与心法。
oneLinerEn: From managing self to others, then managers, a function, a division, the enterprise — each rung demands new work and a new mindset, not just a bigger title.
detail: 拉姆·查兰等提出，领导力的成长是六次“转型”而非单纯升职：管理自我、管理他人(放下亲手做、改通过别人拿结果)、管理管理者(不再亲自带一线、去选带管理者)、管理职能(跳出单一部门做跨职能权衡)、管理业务(兼顾短期与长期、面向外部利益相关者)、管理全集团(定战略与文化、面向资本市场)。它解释了很多“提拔即失败”：岗位变了，人却仍用上一层的活法干，于是各层级都退回做各自旧工作，组织空转。真正的晋升要求工作理念、时间与技能的三重转变。
detailEn: Charan and colleagues cast leadership growth as six transitions rather than mere promotions — managing self, managing others (letting go of hands-on work to get results through people), managing managers (leading leaders instead of the front line), managing a function (cross-functional trade-offs beyond one silo), managing a business (balancing short and long term and outside stakeholders) and managing the enterprise (setting strategy and culture for the markets). It explains many 'promoted-to-failure' cases: the seat changes but the person still works one rung down, so every level does its predecessor's job and the organisation spins idle. Real advancement needs a threefold shift in work values, time application and skills.

oneLiner: 以自知、守底线、表里如一赢得信任:领导者的“真”本身就是影响力。
oneLinerEn: Win trust through self-awareness, a moral core and walking your talk — a leader's realness is itself influence.
detail: 在安然、金融危机等“伪善领导”失信之后,管理学转向研究真诚的领导者。真实型领导四要素:自我觉察(懂自己的强项与盲点)、内化道德观(决策忠于价值观而非迎合外部压力)、平衡地处理信息(先倾听征求再下判断)、关系透明(对下属坦诚、也敢于示弱)。它建立在心理安全感之上,通过言行一致积累“信任账户”,带出高承诺的团队,与仆人式、变革型领导互补。
detailEn: After Enron and the financial crisis eroded trust in inauthentic leaders, the field turned to genuine ones. Authentic leadership has four parts: self-awareness (knowing your strengths and blind spots), an internalised moral perspective (choices true to values, not pleasing outside pressure), balanced processing (hearing and weighing before judging) and relational transparency (candid with followers, willing to show weakness). Built on psychological safety, it accrues a trust account through say-do consistency and yields highly committed teams, complementing servant and transformational leadership.

oneLiner: 除经济、人力、社会资本外,还有一种可开发的“心理资本”:希望、效能、韧性、乐观。
oneLinerEn: Besides economic, human and social capital lies a developable psychological capital — Hope, Efficacy, Resilience, Optimism.
detail: 卢桑斯提出的心理资本用首字拼成 HERO:希望(有目标、有路径、有动力)、自我效能(相信自己能成)、韧性(受挫后反弹)、乐观(把成败作暂时且可改变的解释)。与前三种资本不同,它可以被培养和测量,研究显示高水平心理资本与更高绩效、满意度、留任相关。它给管理者一个抓手:别只投技能培训,也要投资员工的信心、复原力与解释风格。
detailEn: Luthans's psychological capital spells out HERO: hope (goals, pathways and the will to pursue them), self-efficacy (belief you can succeed), resilience (bouncing back after setbacks) and optimism (explaining wins and losses as temporary and changeable). Unlike the other three capitals, it can be developed and measured; high PsyCap correlates with better performance, satisfaction and retention. It hands managers a lever: invest not only in skills but in employees' confidence, recovery and explanatory style.

oneLiner: 好目标该具体、可衡量、能达成、相关、有时限——否则只是句口号。
oneLinerEn: A good goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound — else it is just a slogan.
detail: SMART 是把笼统愿望变成可执行目标的检验清单:Specific 说清到底做什么、Measurable 定下可量化的标准、Achievable 既有挑战又够得着、Relevant 与更大的目标相关、Time-bound 设明确期限。它常被归于乔治·多里奥特等实践者,与洛克“目标设定理论”(具体而困难的目标更能带动绩效)一脉相承,也常用来给 OKR 的关键结果与 KPI 把关。它是把“想做某事”翻译成“怎样才算做成”的通用语法。
detailEn: SMART is a checklist that turns a vague wish into an executable goal — Specific (what exactly), Measurable (the quantified bar), Achievable (stretching yet reachable), Relevant (tied to a larger aim) and Time-bound (a clear deadline). Often credited to Doriot and other practitioners, it rhymes with Locke's goal-setting theory (specific, hard goals drive performance) and is used to vet OKR key results and KPIs. It is the common grammar for translating I want to do X into what counts as done.
